title: Rice, brown, cooked, fat added, NS as to fat type

content.title: About
content.content: Brown rice is a whole‑grain rice that retains its bran layer and germ. When cooked with added fat (oil, butter, or other vegetable fats) it becomes softer and more flavorful. The product is classified as “NS” (not specified) for fat type, meaning detailed fat composition is not provided.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Brown rice retains more fiber, B‑vitamins, and minerals than white rice.
Adding fat raises the calorie content by roughly 20 %.
In Japan and China brown rice is often cooked with a splash of sesame oil for aroma.
Brown rice has a lower glycemic index, helping to stabilize blood sugar levels.
Traditional Asian recipes sometimes use coconut milk, another source of added fat.

items.title: High in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains magnesium and selenium
items.content: These minerals are essential for muscle function, nerve signaling, and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Helps regulate blood sugar
items.content: The low glycemic index helps avoid rapid glucose spikes.

items.title: Provides healthy fats
items.content: Added fat supplies energy and aids absorption of fat‑soluble vitamins.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E acts as an antioxidant, protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: The added fat increases energy density, so portion control is important.

items.title: Fat allergies
items.content: Individuals allergic to certain plant or animal fats may react.

items.title: Arsenic content
items.content: Brown rice can contain trace amounts of arsenic; rinsing before cooking reduces it.

items.title: Not suitable for fat‑free diets
items.content: This product is unsuitable for strict fat‑free eating plans.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked brown rice with added fat can be served as a side dish with meat, fish, or vegetables. It is also used in salads, pilafs, and soups. For a lighter flavor, drizzle a small amount of olive or coconut oil over the rice just before serving.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked rice in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 4‑5 days. For longer storage, freeze portions in freezer‑safe bags. Reheat to at least 75 °C before consumption.
